title: Sample Ratio Mismatch (SRM)
interviewAnswer: SRM occurs when observed treatment/control counts differ unexpectedly from the planned allocation. It is a diagnostic red flag for assignment, logging, eligibility or exposure bugs, so effect estimates should not be trusted until explained.
keyPoints: Test assignment counts against expected proportions.
SRM can signal instrumentation or filtering bugs.
Do not “fix” SRM by reweighting blindly.
why: Sample Ratio Mismatch (SRM) appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
intuition: Test assignment counts against expected proportions.
deepDive: SRM occurs when observed treatment/control counts differ unexpectedly from the planned allocation. It is a diagnostic red flag for assignment, logging, eligibility or exposure bugs, so effect estimates should not be trusted until explained. SRM can signal instrumentation or filtering bugs. Do not “fix” SRM by reweighting blindly. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: A 50/50 experiment producing 60/40 traffic may indicate a broken assignment path for one platform.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.

production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
